dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Thoroughly read helpers.py (multiple passes, lines 1-240 and 1-260), run.sh, and every test_*_public.py file before writing any code; also probed installed packages, finding no web/spreadsheet frameworks and deliberately choosing a stdlib implementation. This is well past a single skim — concrete shape extraction plus a deliberate library decision.

As it reached sort/filter, spill, and pivot subsystems it re-consulted the exact test files to extract precise wire shapes (e.g. step 17: 'the pivot test confirms pivot /cells must be a list of records like {row:[...], value:...}'; sort/filter uses zero-based column indexes with keys column/asc). Contract-driven re-reading as new subsystems are hit — a high-anchor trait.

Reverse-engineered spill coordinate ordering by reproducing the exact B1=SEQUENCE(4) case against the live server and observing ghosts at A2:A5 vs expected B2:B4 — grounding behavior in observed client expectations rather than guessing.

Excel-semantics handling (percent postfix, lazy IFERROR, SQRT-of-negative → #NUM!, self-cycle #CIRC!) was driven reactively by smoke-test failures and the agent's own knowledge, not by proactively probing an Excel/LibreOffice oracle or building an explicit contract reference — the main gap versus levels 8-10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it read helpers.py and run.sh thoroughly, extracted concrete request/response shapes, made a deliberate library choice (stdlib after probing installed packages), and re-consulted the test client repeatedly as it reached new subsystems (sort/filter, spill, pivot, collab) — the contract-driven-throughout behavior of the top anchors. However it falls short of level 8 because it never built an explicit cross-referenced contract map, and its grounding in Excel/LibreOffice ground truth was reactive (fixing sentinels/functions as smoke tests failed and relying on its own knowledge) rather than proactively probing genuinely tricky semantics against an oracle. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Two-phase framing: a recon phase to extract the contract from /dev_tests, then a single monolithic build of the entire server.py at step 9. Building everything at once rather than sequencing checkable sub-goals is the opposite of a milestone hierarchy, though the recon-then-build split is a coarse phasing.
Ran the core API + engine tests FIRST before the full suite — a sensible rough dependency ordering (core cell/engine correctness gated before breadth), showing some deliberate staging.

Fixes proceed in logically clustered stages (engine funcs → self-cycle/deps → LET/LAMBDA → spill/dynamic arrays → collab → pivot/locale), with each test run acting as the checkpoint. Ordering is reactive to failure clusters rather than a pre-planned dependency/risk hierarchy.
Completion criterion is entirely the provided smoke suite ('131 passed'); done-checks are runnable tests but are the supplied suite, not self-defined per-milestone criteria.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent phases the work into sensible stages (contract recon → monolithic core build → engine-first test gate → full-suite fix clusters) with test runs as rough per-stage checkpoints, matching the level-5 anchor. It does not reach level 8: the primary strategy was building the whole surface at once (step 9) and then fixing whatever the smoke suite flagged, rather than an explicit dependency/risk-ordered milestone hierarchy that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (graph/spill/recompute) with self-defined done-criteria. The mild dependency awareness (engine before breadth) lifts it above a flat to-do list (3), landing it at 5.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Runs dev_tests/run.sh and targeted subsets (test_api, test_engine) regularly, using failures to drive formula-engine fixes — core smoke-suite-driven loop.

Writes ad-hoc urllib/python scripts against the live server to hand-check specific outputs (SEQUENCE ghost coordinates B2:B4 vs A2:A5, BYROW, self-cycle) — genuine hand-verification of expected Excel values, but each reproduces a failing smoke-suite case rather than extending coverage beyond it.

Notes `requests` unavailable and falls back to urllib for manual probing; no openpyxl xlsx round-trip check, no independent Excel/LibreOffice oracle, no performance benchmarking against the stated bounds.

Final verification is 'full public suite = 131 passed', then submits as complete — treats a green smoke run as done despite spec's warning that grading is a much larger hidden suite plus LibreOffice cell-by-cell comparison.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs the smoke suite regularly and repeatedly hand-checks specific formula/spill/collab outputs against expected Excel values via manual urllib scripts, which matches the level-5 anchor. However, all self-built checks merely reproduce smoke-suite scenarios to diagnose failures — there is no targeted testing beyond the suite: no openpyxl xlsx round-trip verification, no error-sentinel/spill-collision probing beyond what tests cover, no performance benchmarks against the explicit bounds, and no independent Excel/LibreOffice oracle. It ultimately equates a green visible suite with completion, keeping it squarely at 5 rather than 8.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: After first engine run, enumerates the exact set of missing functions/syntax from failures (percent, LOG/SIGN/PRODUCT, *IFS, concat, lazy IFERROR, SQRT neg, ISTEXT) — a granular but test-derived remaining list.
Reconciles against suite results ('104 passing, 27 failing') and clusters remaining work into accurate feature categories (spill, LET/LAMBDA, collab, pivot, locale, XLSX).

Maintains a running 'remaining failures' picture and detects a possible stale/false-failure ('spill tests unexpectedly fail even though earlier manual SEQUENCE worked... may be from pre-patch server'), choosing to re-test rather than loop — stuck-state detection and adjustment.

Uses the visible suite pass count ('131 passed') as its completion signal — tracking is bounded by the smoke suite, with no independent ledger of the full ~150-function/15-family surface or hidden coverage.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps an accurate, category-clustered picture of done-vs-remaining that is continuously reconciled against verification results (test pass/fail counts and manual urllib checks), and it detects one stale/stuck state and re-tests rather than looping — behaviors above anchor 5. However, its picture is almost entirely driven by what the visible smoke suite reports; it never maintains an independent granular ledger of the full function catalog or endpoint families (done/partial/not-started) and does not track the hidden surface, falling short of anchor 8's live granular ledger. This places it at a 6, between the checklist (5) and granular-ledger-with-stuck-detection (8) anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Diagnosed that the naive `=`-operator string replacement was corrupting quoted strings and that lazy IFERROR was falsely triggering circular-reference detection by reusing the current cell in the stack — reworked both mechanisms rather than patching symptoms.
Recognized LET pair-loop was reversed and user-defined lambda variable calls were being wrongly uppercased; revised the transform_special design instead of adding local hacks.

Root-cause diagnosis of spill failures: identified coordinate swap (split_ref row/col vs col/row) in materialize_spill and that eval-created lambdas couldn't resolve SUM because env was passed only as locals — fixed the underlying model, and used manual urllib probes to distinguish real failures from stale pre-patch runs.

A patch introduced a 500 regression ('errflag not defined') across most cell patches; agent traced it via server log and grep and fixed the out-of-scope insertion — reactive correction of a self-inflicted derailment.

After full suite showed 27 failures, correctly clustered them by root cause (blank-cell handling, sort/filter request shape, collab welcome shape, locale) and inspected exact contracts before reworking, rather than blind local edits.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognized that failures signaled wrong underlying assumptions — spill coordinate ordering, lambda global scoping, operator replacement inside strings, reversed LET binding order — and reworked the relevant design rather than piling on local patches, matching anchor 8. It also used targeted manual probes to distinguish genuine failures from stale-run artifacts. It falls short of 10 because it introduced a broad 500 regression from its own patch and operated largely reactively off the smoke suite rather than detecting divergence early and proactively.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Chose to build one self-contained server covering the entire surface at once (persistence, REST, formula evaluator, CSV/XLSX, WebSocket collab, SPA) — a breadth-first construction that inherently spreads coverage across all endpoint families rather than rabbit-holing one feature.

Explicitly frames a 'pragmatic implementation covering visible and likely hidden cases' — some awareness of the hidden suite, but no concrete plan for which niches to defer or where marginal effort pays off.

Uses the visible formula list to prioritize and patches a batch of common missing functions (percent, LOG/SIGN/PRODUCT, *IFS, concat, IFERROR) together — coverage decisions are driven by what the smoke suite flags, i.e. high-frequency features first, but reactively rather than via deliberate graded-return reasoning.

Once all 131 visible tests pass, the agent immediately submits with no further breadth expansion or timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas for the hidden suite — no revisited allocation strategy, so it caps below the top anchors.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's coverage was broad by construction (a whole-surface server) and it roughly prioritized high-frequency functions/endpoints via the visible tests, matching the level-5 anchor. It showed only thin, non-actionable awareness of the hidden suite and no explicit breadth-vs-depth trade-off, conscious deferral of low-yield niches, or reallocation as verification progressed — so it falls short of the explicit graded-return reasoning at level 8. Allocation was largely test-driven and stopped the moment visible tests passed, placing it solidly at 5.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
